sections.heading: 1. Single-leg sit-to-stand
lines: ① Stand on one leg in front of a high chair.
② Sit down slowly, stand up slowly.
③ 6–8 reps per side, hold a bench if needed.
④ Easier? Lower the chair or slow it down.

caption:
Momo does squats every day, yet one leg still wobbles on the stairs.

Walking, stairs and running mostly happen on one leg at a time. In two-leg moves like a squat, the stronger side can quietly take more of the load, which is why clinical Pilates often works one side at a time, building strength and balance together.

Hybi's 1-minute check: single-leg sit-to-stand from a high chair, 6–8 reps per side, holding a bench if needed. Notice which side feels harder.

Small differences are normal. A clearly weaker leg after an injury, or pain during single-leg work, is worth an assessment first. Book online via the link in bio
